claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! I'm happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18, which is over the age of 16, there are specific rules that apply. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit for a child under 20 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He actually works full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand a bit more about Alex's work situation.

**How many hours per week does Alex work in his full-time job?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He works full-time, so that's around 24 hours a week or more.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Does Alex receive any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to complete my assessment, I need to confirm a couple more details:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the rules, when a child turns 16 or over, you can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if they are under 20 and stay in approved education or training. However, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 18, works 24 hours or more per week, and is not in approved education or training, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

The reason is that Alex is 18 years old and working full-time (24 hours or more per week) without being in approved education or training. According to the Child Benefit rules, payments stop when a child aged 16 or over starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he returns to education or training, or reduces his working hours—you may be able to claim again, so it's worth keeping that in mind.

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding Child Benefit?
